text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime Minister Alfred Sant says the Maltese government is to send a diplomatic note to all European Union member governments explaining Malta's stand on EU membership and insisting Malta is not anti-EU though it will no longer seek membership.

- Former prime minister Edward Fenech Adami told a radio interviewer that the European Union position of the new Labour government threatened to raise problems in Malta's links with the EU. Fenech Adami, whose government applied for membership, said the fact that the country was no longer seeking this meant it would be treated differently by the EU.

- Prime Minister Alfred Sant returns from Rome. Sant on his first overseas trip as prime minister attended the FAO world food summit and had meetings with several heads of government, including Irish Prime Minister John Bruton and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

- Nationalist Party considers opening television station. The party lost the October 26 election and many supporters blame this on the party's lack of a TV station in contrast to the Labour Party, granted a TV licence by the then nationalist government two years ago.
